taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Anthropic reports concealment and safeguard-evasion tactics, but the preserved occurrence does not establish a monitoring control required for this conduct, a distinct observation-coverage gap, or that such a gap materially degraded detection or intervention. baseline_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Required Governance Routing must remain valid across the material pathway described by the preserved occurrence evidence.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Cross-session splitting and concealment may fragment the context seen by safeguards, but the record does not identify a defined mandatory governance route or control point that successful requests reached execution by bypassing through an alternate path. Required Governance Routing is therefore not established.

baseline_clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic stated that safeguards blocked many requests but not all, while the actors hid their goals and split work across sessions.
baseline_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Anthropic reports that safeguards blocked many weapons-development requests but not all. The record does not establish that an applicable control validly became operative on the same successful requests and then produced an insufficient effect; successful assistance could instead reflect non-activation, fragmented context, a different trigger state, or another path. Control Effectiveness Integrity therefore remains unresolved.

explicit_evidence_changes.baseline: Anthropic reports that likely freelance Russia-based threat actors used Claude Code as part of an effort to develop a full-stack autonomous first-person-view kamikaze drone swarm called DronDoc or Serafim. According to Anthropic, Claude was used to write and test project code for shared swarm memory, fault-tolerant coordination logic, an onboard small language model governing attack, observation and return-to-base behaviours, terminal guidance and detonation logic, control-link geolocation, passive acoustic detection and low-level programmable-chip logic. Anthropic assessed the resulting systems at Technology Readiness Level 3-4: validated in simulation, with code loaded onto real boards, but did not report an operational fielded swarm or casualties resulting from the system. Anthropic states that safeguards blocked many requests but not all, that the actors used concealment and session-splitting tactics to evade safeguards, and that associated accounts were disrupted.
explicit_evidence_changes.candidate: Anthropic reports that likely freelance Russia-based threat actors used Claude Code as part of an effort to develop a full-stack autonomous first-person-view kamikaze drone swarm called DronDoc or Serafim. According to Anthropic, Claude was used to write and test project code for shared swarm memory, fault-tolerant coordination logic, an onboard small language model governing attack, observation and return-to-base behaviours, terminal guidance and detonation logic, control-link geolocation, passive acoustic detection and low-level programmable-chip logic. Anthropic assessed the resulting systems at Technology Readiness Level 3-4: validated in simulation, with code loaded onto real boards, but did not report an operational fielded swarm or casualties resulting from the system.  Anthropic identifies nine associated accounts, eight used only for ordinary freelance work. The actors routed traffic through commercial virtual private servers to evade geographic access restrictions. The provider reports banning associated accounts after investigation. It could not verify the actors’ claimed institutional funding.

baseline.factual_basis: Anthropic's September 2026 threat-intelligence report directly identifies GTG-27005, describes the actors as likely freelance and Russia-based, identifies Claude Code as a development tool, enumerates the software subsystems built with Claude assistance, and assesses the observed systems at TRL 3-4. The same report states that conventional-weapons actors used tactics including concealment and splitting work across sessions to evade safeguards, and that safeguards blocked many requests but not all. Anthropic's separate September 2026 conventional-weapons capability evaluation provides broader corroborating evidence that frontier models can materially assist tactical targeting and conventional-weapons engineering tasks, but it does not independently establish the GTG-27005 occurrence.
baseline.governance_interpretation: The provider reports successful coding assistance in lethal-weapons development and later account disruption. These support a harmful-query and security failure, followed by a bounded mitigation and documented investigation. No fielded swarm, casualties, autonomous project initiation or particular internal control state is established.
baseline.significance_to_cam: GTG-27005 is governance-relevant because it demonstrates that safety controls can face sustained, distributed evasion across sessions while an AI coding agent contributes directly to a complex weapons-development workflow. It also exposes a boundary between successful model assistance, misuse prevention, and occurrence-level harm: a system can materially contribute to dangerous engineering activity even when the public evidence does not establish downstream deployment or casualties.
assessment_boundaries: Anthropic describes the actors as likely freelance and Russia-based; the public evidence does not establish that they were acting on behalf of the Russian state.
Actor claims of support or funding by Russian institutions are not treated as verified attribution.
Anthropic reports TRL 3-4, simulation validation and code loaded onto real boards; it does not establish an operationally fielded autonomous swarm.
No casualties, physical strikes, property destruction or battlefield effects caused by the GTG-27005 system are established in the reviewed evidence.
The exact Claude model versions used in every GTG-27005 session are not established at occurrence-level granularity in the reviewed disclosure.
The record does not infer that every software component described by Anthropic was generated solely by Claude or that the actors lacked independent engineering capability.

Those occurrence facts are governance-significant, but Alignment Taxonomy 0.6.9 does not provide a content/harm class for weapons-development assistance itself, and the preserved control-state evidence does not establish Monitoring Coverage Integrity, Required Governance Routing, or Control Effectiveness Integrity without inferring missing implementation facts. FC-000023 and FC-000041 are therefore rejected; FC-000083 remains unresolved. No canonical Incident classification is forced.
